Ibrahim ibn Shurayk narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, he said: Salam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, he said: Harun ibn Kabir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-A'la, Allah will grant him the reward of ten good deeds for each letter that Allah the Glorified revealed to Ibrahim, Musa and Muhammad" [129] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/326.]].

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, he said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Aban narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he recited "Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A'la," would say:

"Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la" [130] [['Awn al-Ma'bud: 3/98.]]. Similarly, it is narrated from Ali, Ubayy, Musa, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they used to do likewise.

And Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak that he used to say this, and he used to say: whoever recites it should recite it in this manner.

It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved this surah, "Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A'la." The first to say "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la" was Mika'il. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"O Jibril, inform me about the reward of one who says it in his prayer or outside his prayer." He said: "O Muhammad, there is no believing man or woman who says it in his prostration or outside his prostration except that it will be heavier in his scale than the Throne, the Footstool and the mountains of the world. And Allah the Glorified and Exalted says: 'My servant has spoken truly; I am Most High above everything, and there is nothing above Me. Bear witness, My angels, that I have forgiven My servant and admitted him to My Garden.' When he dies, Mika'il visits him every day. When it is the Day of Resurrection, he carries him on his wing and stands him before Allah the Glorified, and he says: 'O Lord, intercede for him,' and He says: 'I have interceded for him; take him to the Garden.'"

Qabisa ibn Amir said: When "Fasabbih bismi Rabbika al-'Azim" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Put it in your bowing." Then when "Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A'la" was revealed, he (ﷺ) said: "Put it in your prostration" [132] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/326.]] [133] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/326.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A'la" means: say, "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la." This interpretation was adopted by a group of the Companions and the Successors. Others said its meaning is: exalt your Lord, the Most High, above what the atheists say about Him and what the falsifiers attribute to Him. They took "isim" as a supplementary particle. It may also mean: exalt the essence of your Lord above what is not fitting for Him, because "ism," "dhat" and "nafs" all express existence and affirmation.

Others said: exalt the naming of your Lord and your mention of Him; you mention Him only while humble and reverent, and respectful of His remembrance. They took "ism" to mean "tasmiya" (naming). Al-Farra' said: whether you say "Sabbih isma Rabbika" or "sabbih bi-ism Rabbika," if you intend His remembrance and glorification, it is the same. Ibn Abbas said: pray by the command of your Lord, the Most High.

"Alladhi khalaqa fasawwa": He created and proportioned, so He made the creation balanced. "Wa alladhi qaddara":

Ali, al-Sulami and al-Kisa'i lightened the dal, while others doubled it.

"Fahada": Mujahid said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, and to happiness and wretchedness, and He guided the cattle to their pastures. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: He made His creatures know how the male comes to the female. It is narrated from Ata', who said: He gave every animal what suits it, and this is its state. It was also said: He guided them to the acquisition of provision and livelihood. It was also said: He created benefits in things and guided man to the way of extracting them. It was also said: He guided to His religion whomever of His creatures He wills.

al-Suddi said: He determined the child's duration in the womb as nine months, less or more, and guided it to exit from the womb.

al-Wasiti said: He determined happiness and wretchedness for them, then facilitated for each of those who are destined for it the path to what was decreed for him. It was also said: He decreed provision and guided them to seek it. It was also said: He decreed sins for His servants, then guided them to repentance.

"Wa alladhi akhraja al-mar'a": the plants, of green, yellow, red and white.

"Faja'alahu ghuthaean": dry, crumbled, decayed. "Ahwa": black, when it dries and ages.

"Sanuqri'uka": We will teach you, and Jibril will recite to you. "Fala tansa illa ma sha'a Allah": except what Allah wills that you forget, and that is what He abrogates of the Qur'an. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: When Jibril descended with the Qur'an, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would not finish the last part of the verse before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began speaking its beginning, for fear of forgetting it. So Allah the Exalted revealed: "Sanuqri'uka fala tansa," and after that he forgot nothing.

The exception in this interpretation, as al-Farra' said, is: he did not will to forget anything. It is like His saying, the Exalted: "Khalidina fiha ma damati al-samawatu wal-ard illa ma sha'a Rabbuka" [[Surat Hud: 107.]]. And you say in speech, "I will surely give you everything you ask, except what he wills of withholding from you," while the intention is that he will not withhold. On this principle, oaths are qualified by an exception, and the intention of the swearer is the exception.

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Baghdadi say:

I heard Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Farghani say: Al-Junayd's assembly was frequented by the people of devotion and the people of learning, and among those who frequented him was Ibn Kaysan the grammarian, who was in his time a distinguished man. He said to him one day: "O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about His saying, the Glorified: 'Sanuqri'uka fala tansa'?" He answered him quickly, as if the question had been prepared for him some time before: "Do not forget to act upon it." Ibn Kaysan was greatly impressed by him and said: "May Allah never break your mouth; a man like you speaks from his own judgment" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/19.]].

"Innahu ya'lamu al-jahra" from speech and deeds, "wa ma yakhfa": Muhammad ibn Hamid said: He knows the public and the secret giving of charity. "Wa nuyassiruka lil-yusra": to the work of Paradise. It was also said: it is connected to the earlier speech, meaning: We know what is loud of what you recite, O Muhammad, to Jibril when he finishes reciting to you, and "wa ma yakhfa": what you recite to yourself for fear of forgetting it. Then He promised him, saying: "Wa nuyassiruka lil-yusra," meaning: the revelation will be made easy for you, so that you memorize it, teach it and act upon it. It was also said: and He will grant you success in the easy Shari'a, which is the tolerant monotheism (al-hanifiyya al-samha).

"Fadhakkir": admonish with the Qur'an, "in nafa'ati al-dhikra": if the reminder benefits. "Sayadhdhakkaru": will be admonished, "man yakhsha": whoever fears Allah the Glorified. "Yatajannabuha": "yatajannabuha" means: and he avoids the reminder and keeps far from it.

"Al-ashqa": the wretched one in Allah's knowledge. "Alladhi yasla al-nar al-kubra": who will burn in the greatest Fire, "thumma la yamutu fiha" so as to rest, "wa la yahya": a life that benefits him.

I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn Abdullah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz say:

Ibn Ata said: "La yahya": so he may rest from separation, "wa la yahya": so he may reach the spirit of union.

ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar reported from Nāfiʿ, who said: When Ibn ʿUmar had prayed the morning prayer (meaning on the day of ʿId), he would say: "O Nāfiʿ, have you given out the charity?"
